Rashi on Shabbat 152a:10:1.hebrew: שטוף - כמו סוס שוטף במלחמה (ירמיהו ח׳:ו׳), להוט אחר הדבר ורודף:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:10:1.english: Steeped - Like “a horse rushing into battle” (Jeremiah 8:6), eager for the matter and pursuing [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:10:2.hebrew: וטעם זקנים יקח - וע"כ מדקשי קראי אהדדי, חד מתוקם בחכמים וחד בזקני השוק:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:10:2.english: And takes away the understanding of the aged - And perforce, since the verses contradict each other, one is established [as referring] to scholars and one to elders of the marketplace.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:11:1.hebrew: מגבוה ייראו - יראים הם הזקנים מגבשושית שבדרכים, ואומרים גבוהים הם:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:11:1.english: They shall be afraid of [that which is] high - The elderly are afraid of a knoll on the roads, and say [that] they are high.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:11:3.hebrew: וינאץ השקד - אילן של שקדים יציץ, ויהיו בולטין נצים שלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:11:3.english: And the almond tree shall blossom - An almond tree will blossom, and its buds will protrude.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:11:4.hebrew: זו קליבוסת - עצם של הנק"א שהירך תקוע בו, בולט ויוצא מרוב תשות כחו:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:11:4.english: This is kelivoset - The hip bone into which the thigh is inserted protrudes and sticks out from the great weakness of his strength.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:11:5.english: And the grasshopper shall drag itself along - [It] seems to him like a burden of a heavy load.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:11:6.hebrew: ותפר האביונה - תבטל התאוה, חמדת תשמיש:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:11:6.english: And the caper berry shall fail - Desire, [namely] sexual desire, will cease.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:12:1.english: Reciting a section - Reciting sections of verses in order.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:12:2.english: He drew [a breath] and sighed - [It was] Rav.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:12:4.hebrew: זו אשה - אם לא על פי גזרת המלך, לא היתה ראויה להתאוות לה, שהיא כחמת מלאה מיאוס, והכל רצים אחריה:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:12:4.english: This is a woman - Were it not for the decree of the King [i.e., God], she would not be fit to be desired, for she is like a flask full of filth, and [yet] everyone runs after her.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:13:1.hebrew: מדור לפי כבודו - מדלא כתיב אל בית העולם, ש"מ כל אחד ואחד לבית המוכן לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:13:1.english: A dwelling place in accordance with his honor - Since it is not written "to the eternal home" [but rather "his eternal home"], learn from this [that] each and every one [goes] to the home prepared for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:13:2.english: Through a single gate - So too here, all die in the same manner.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:14:1.english: That a person does in his youth - Excessive sexual intercourse.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:14:2.english: Darken his face - [It] weakens his strength.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:16:1.english: Who has no comforters - He has no mourners whom [people] would need to comfort.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:16:2.english: In his place - In the place where he died.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:1:1.english: Of the bathroom - [Tears shed] out of pain.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:1:2.english: Of produce - Such as the smell of mustard.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:2:1.english: The flanks - Les flancs [the flanks, in Old French].

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:2:2.english: And the ribs - For they guard the internal organs and a person's vitality, and close around them.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:2:3.english: These are the legs - For a person's strength is supported upon them.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:3:1.english: To the House of Avidan - A place made for Sadducees and Boethusians to debate with Israel about [Scriptural] verses.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:3:2.hebrew: טור תלג - ההר נעשה שלג, כלומר ראשי לבן:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:3:2.english: A mountain of snow - The mountain has become snow, meaning my head is white.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:3:3.hebrew: סחרוני גלידין - סביבותיו של הר מלאו קרח, כלומר שפמי וזקני הלבינו:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:3:3.english: Its surroundings are ice - The surroundings of the mountain are filled with ice; that is to say, my mustache and my beard have turned white.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:3:4.english: His dogs do not bark - My voice is not heard.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:3:6.hebrew: אדלא אבידנא בחישנא - אחר מה שלא אבד ממני אני מפשפש. מרוב זקנה אני הולך שחוח ומנענע, ונראה כמי שמבקש דינר הנאבד לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:3:6.english: For what I have not lost, I am searching - For that which was not lost from me, I am searching. Because of great old age, I walk bent over and swaying, and appear like one who is seeking a dinar that was lost to him.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:4:1.hebrew: תרתי טבא מתלת - טובים ב' הרגלים של ימי בחרות מג' של זקנה, שצריך משענת עם רגליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:4:1.english: Two are better than three - The two legs of [one's] days of youth are better than [the] three of old age, when [one] needs a staff with his legs.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:4:2.hebrew: ווי לה - חבל עליה, כלומר יש לו להתאונן ולצעוק ווי, ההולכת ואינה חוזרת:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:4:2.english: Woe to it - Alas for it, meaning one ought to lament and cry out "woe" [for] that which goes and does not return.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:4:3.english: A crown of roses - A crown of roses.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:4:5.hebrew: דוק בככי ותשכח בניגרי - אכול הרבה ותמצא האכילה בפסיעותיך, שיחזק כחך. דוק — כמו אכלה מדקה (דניאל ז׳:י״ט), לשון כוסס:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:4:5.english: Grind with [your] teeth and you will find [it] in [your] steps - Eat much, and you will find [the benefit of] the eating in your steps, for your strength will be strengthened. "Dok" is like "okhlah madakah" [“devouring and crushing”] (Daniel 7:19), an expression of chewing.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:4:6.english: Untie your sack - Open your mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:5:1.english: Goza - He was a eunuch and a Sadducee.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:5:2.hebrew: מהכא לקרחינא כמה הוי - כמה מהלך יש מכאן עד הקרח, ולהקניטו על קרחתו נתכוון:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:5:2.english: From here to Karḥina, how [far] is it - How much of a journey is there from here to the bald one? And he intended to taunt him about his baldness.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:5:3.english: Like from here to Gozanya - Like [the distance] from here to the eunuch.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:5:4.hebrew: אמר ליה צדוקי ברחא קרחא בארבעה - שהקרח לקוח בארבע. ברחא קרחא הוא עז; על שם שאינו מלובש בצמר כרחל, קרוי קרחא:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:5:4.english: The Sadducee said to him: A bald buck [is sold] for four - For the bald one is bought for four. Barcha karcha is a goat; because it is not clothed in wool like a ewe, it is called karcha [bald].

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:5:5.english: He said to him - Rabbi Yehoshua.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:5:6.hebrew: עיקרא שליפא - שה שביציו עקורים ונתוקין, לוקחין בשמנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:5:6.english: Ikkara shelifa - A sheep [or goat] whose testicles are uprooted and torn off, they buy [it] for eight [dinars].

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:6:1.english: He saw him - A Sadducee [saw] Rabbi Yehoshua, that he was not wearing his shoes.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:6:2.hebrew: קרחא מצויינא - אתה הקרח, במריבה אתה באת עמדי? בתמיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:6:2.english: Bald one, do you quarrel? - You, the bald one, have you come [to engage] with me in a quarrel? [This is said] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:6:3.hebrew: אמר לו רבי יהושע עיקרא שליפא תוכחה - אתה הסריס, להקניטני ולהתווכח עמי באת:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:6:3.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: [Does] a castrated male goat [speak words of] rebuke? - You, the eunuch, have come to taunt me and to argue with me?

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:7:1.hebrew: לא הקבלנו פניך - לא הקבלת פני, ודרך ענוה קאמר ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:7:1.english: We did not greet you - You did not greet me, and he said [this] to him out of humility.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:7:2.english: Rocks - Small [rocks] have become tall, for I have grown old.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:7:3.english: [Places that are] near - Seem to me as distant.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:7:4.english: Two have become three for me - For I need a staff.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:7:5.english: That which brings peace to the house - [the] organ of marital relations.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:7:6.hebrew: לישנא אחרינא: קרובים נעשו רחוקים - מרוב חלשות של אדם כשמזקין, צריך להרחיק רגליו זה מזה:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:7:6.english: Another explanation: [Things that were] near have become far - Because of a person's great weakness when he grows old, he must spread his feet apart from one another.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:8:1.english: That does not grind - [Meaning] that his intestines do not grind his food.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:8:2.english: Stomach - [This] is the omasum, which they call centpels [in Old French, i.e., manyplies].

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:8:3.english: All the daughters of song - All sounds of song are [like] conversation to him.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:9:1.hebrew: שדעתן של זקנים משתנות - דכתיב האדע בין טוב לרע, ובזקנה מרובה קאמר:
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:9:1.english: That the minds of the elderly change - For it is written, "Can I discern between good and bad?" — and [it] speaks of advanced old age.

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:9:2.hebrew: מתרפטות - מתבקעות, כמו מנעל המרופט (לעיל שבת דף קמא:):
Rashi on Shabbat 152a:9:2.english: Become cracked - [They] split open, like a worn-out shoe (above, Shabbat 141b).

Rashi on Shabbat 152a:9:3.english: Become heavy - Like “and make his ears heavy” (Isaiah 6).
